music.title: Apollo et Hyacinthus
music.description: Mozart's Latin school opera casts Oebalus as Hyacinthus' father at the Spartan court — the king who mourns when Apollo's discus kills his son. The libretto keeps the Oebalid genealogy that made Hyacinthus an Oebalides in Roman poetry.

popCulture.title: Oebalus
popCulture.description: King of Sparta, father of Tyndareus, Icarius, and Hippocoon — the stem from which Helen, the Dioscuri, and Penelope descend as Oebalids.

popCulture.title: Tyndareus
popCulture.description: Oebalus' son who holds the Spartan throne and fosters Helen and the Dioscuri — the Oebalid house at the hinge of the Trojan War.

popCulture.title: Oebalides
popCulture.description: Roman poets call Spartans and Helen's line Oebalides after Oebalus — the king's name as shorthand for Lacedaemon.

popCulture.title: Hyacinthus
popCulture.description: Often styled an Oebalid — Apollo's Spartan beloved claimed as Oebalus' son in some genealogies and on Mozart's stage.
